title: Azure SQL Managed Instance
description: Configure Azure SQL Managed Instance for near-full SQL Server compatibility and hybrid cloud workloads.

data.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance is a fully managed database engine that delivers near-complete SQL Server compatibility while offloading infrastructure maintenance, patching, and high availability to Microsoft. It supports instance-level features such as SQL Server Agent, cross-database queries, Service Broker, CLR integration, and Distributed Transactions, making it the natural migration target for existing on-premises SQL Server applications that need minimal code changes before moving to the cloud.

cards.title: Azure SQL Database
cards.description: Single database or elastic pool with maximum isolation. Best for new cloud-native applications that do not need instance-level features.

cards.title: Azure SQL Managed Instance
cards.description: Near-full SQL Server compatibility in a managed PaaS offering. Ideal for migrating existing SQL Server applications with minimal changes.
pros: SQL Agent, cross-database queries, and CLR support
cons: Slower scaling than Azure SQL Database

cards.title: SQL Server on Azure VM
cards.description: Full SQL Server installed on an Azure Virtual Machine. Maximum control over the operating system and SQL Server version.
cons: You manage OS patches and backups

data.title: Instance-Level Features Supported
items: SQL Server Agent: schedule jobs, alerts, and operators for routine maintenance.
Cross-database queries: three-part naming and elastic queries between databases in the same instance.
Service Broker: asynchronous message processing between databases.
CLR Integration: run .NET assemblies inside the database engine.
Distributed Transactions: MSDTC support for coordinated commits across databases and resources.
Database Mail: send email directly from the database engine.
Filestream and FileTable: store unstructured data in the file system with transactional consistency.

data.text: Managed Instance is deployed inside a dedicated subnet within an Azure Virtual Network. It uses an Always On Availability Group internally to provide high availability with automatic failover, eliminating the need for manual Windows Server Failover Clustering configuration. The instance exposes a public endpoint for management traffic, but all user database traffic can be routed through private IP addresses for zero-trust networking.

data.title: Subnet Sizing
data.text: Managed Instance reserves a minimum of 31 IP addresses in the subnet for its infrastructure. Plan your subnet CIDR block carefully because you cannot shrink it later, and you cannot reuse the subnet for other resources.

You can deploy Managed Instance through the Azure Portal, Azure CLI, PowerShell, or ARM Templates. Choose the General Purpose tier for most business workloads and the Business Critical tier for applications that require low latency, high IO, and in-memory OLTP.

Because Managed Instance lives inside a VNet, client applications must have network reachability to the instance subnet. You can use Azure Private Link or native VNet peering to connect without traversing the public internet. Connection strings point to the managed instance fully qualified domain name, and port 1433 must be open between the client and the subnet network security group.

data.text: Managed Instance supports both SQL authentication and Azure Active Directory authentication. AD authentication eliminates password-based connections for users and applications and supports features such as conditional access, identity protection, and just-in-time access. Use AD authentication as the default wherever possible.

data.title: Managed Instance Security Features
items: Azure AD authentication and contained database users.
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with service-managed or customer-managed keys.
Always Encrypted with secure enclaves for rich computations on encrypted data.
Vulnerability Assessment: scans for misconfigurations and security holes.
Advanced Threat Protection: detects SQL injection, anomalous logins, and brute-force attacks.
Auditing to Log Analytics, Storage, or Event Hubs for compliance reporting.

data.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance exposes the same core DMVs as on-premises SQL Server, such as sys.dm_exec_requests and sys.dm_os_wait_stats, plus Azure-specific DMVs for resource governance. You can route logs to Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, or Storage for long-term retention. Automatic tuning still applies at the database level, and backup management is fully automated with configurable retention periods.

data.title: Built-in Health Monitoring
data.text: Monitor the managed instance health using the sys.dm_os_cluster_nodes DMV to verify replica quorum, and use the maintenance window feature to control when platform updates occur, minimizing disruption to production workloads.

data.title: Ideal Scenarios
items: Lift-and-shift migrations of existing SQL Server databases with minimal application changes.
Applications that rely on SQL Server Agent for scheduled jobs or reporting.
Systems that require cross-database queries or distributed transactions.
Organizations that need VNet isolation and private networking for regulatory compliance.
Workloads that need SQL Server compatibility features not available in Azure SQL Database.

data.title: Cost and Sizing
data.text: Managed Instance is priced per instance, not per database, and the minimum compute and storage allocation is higher than a single Azure SQL Database. Evaluate total cost of ownership carefully, including backup storage and egress charges, before choosing Managed Instance for a small number of small databases.

data.title: Managed Instance Key Points
points: Managed Instance provides near 100 percent SQL Server compatibility in a PaaS model.
It supports instance-level features including SQL Agent, cross-database queries, CLR, and Distributed Transactions.
Deploy inside a dedicated VNet subnet for private, secure networking.
Choose General Purpose for typical workloads or Business Critical for low-latency, high IO requirements.
Use Azure AD authentication, TDE, and Vulnerability Assessment to harden security.
Monitor with DMVs, Azure Monitor, and Log Analytics; use maintenance windows to control updates.
Best suited for lift-and-shift migrations and applications that need SQL Server instance features.
data.takeaway: Azure SQL Managed Instance bridges the gap between on-premises SQL Server and the cloud, offering PaaS convenience with the compatibility required to migrate existing applications without rewriting core logic.
